sets: Ambulance / Bus Lane / Zig Zag lines
q: To check 'blind spot' when driving, you must
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Turn your head and look into the wing mirrors .
Turn your head and look into the rear-view mirror.
Before changing lanes, you should check your blind spots by
Looking into the rear view mirror.
Looking over your shoulder.
Looking at the side mirrors.
'Blind spots' of a vehicle is an area which cannot be viewed by
the rear view mirror.
left and right wings mirror.
both A and B.
Motorcyclist will often look over their right shoulder just before turning right. This is because ___
they need to listen for following traffic.
they need to check for traffic in their blind area.
looking around helps them balance as they turn.
Before you make a U-turn on the road, you should check your blind spot by
looking at the rear view mirror.
looking over your shoulder.
looking at the side mirrors.
It is important to check the 'blind spot' before
changing lanes.
changing gear.
slowing down.
Your reaction time could be affected when
you are tired.
your vehicle is old.
the traffic is heavy.
When driving through puddles of water on the road, you should
drive faster.
drive slower.
not change speed.
Before moving off, you should
use your mirrors and signal if necessary.
use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal.
signal and move.
How does the car interior lights affect your driving?
It makes you more alert.
It reduces your visibility.
It helps you to see better.
On a wet road, the braking distance will
not increase if the tyres are good.
not increase if the brakes are efficient.
increase despite good tyres.
In which of these situations should you avoid overtaking?
Approaching a dip in the road.
On a 50km/h road.
In a one-way street.
What should you use the horn for?
to signal your annoyance.
to greet other road users.
to warn others of danger.
When driving in heavy rain, you should turn on
The hazard lights.
The headlights and hazard lights.
The headlights and tail lights.
You must signal your intention at least
2 seconds in advance.
3 seconds in advance.
5 seconds in advance.
When you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle, you should
Stop immediately where you are in order to make way.
Pull over to the left or right side of the road.
Sound your horn to warn the front vehicles to speed up.
Within the zig-zag lines area of a pedestrian crossing, you;
May overtake another vehicle only when that vehicle comes to a complete stop.
May overtake another vehicle if you do not cause inconvenience to pedestrians.
Must not overtake even if you think it is safe to do so.
When you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle but are not sure where it is coming from, you should
continue to drive at the same speed.
move to the side and stop if necessary.
drive faster so as not to obstruct the emergency vehicle.
You should give way to emergency vehicles approaching from behind by
slowing down.
moving to the side.
driving faster.
When an emergency vehicle behind you sounds its siren, you should
slow down quickly.
pull to the side and stop if necessary.
increase your speed.
During bus lane prohibited hours, motorist is allowed to use the bus lane when
it is empty.
the other lanes are congested.
the driver is trying to avoid a collision.
If a fire engine behind you sounds the siren, you should
Continue at normal speed.
Move to the side, slow down or stop if necessary.
Increase your speed and move to the side.
On a one way street, you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle behind you, you should
Give way by moving to the left only.
Give way by moving to the left or right.
Stop immediately.
What must you do when a police vehicle with its siren on is behind you?
Continue to drive as normal.
Slow down and move to the side.
Speed up.
When being followed by a police vehicle with its siren on, you should
Accelerate quickly to get away from it.
Pull over safely, as soon as possible to let it pass.
Brake quickly and stop to let it pass.
On Saturday, all vehicles must avoid the bus lane between (red marking)
7.30 am to 8.00 pm
7.30 am to 11.00 pm
5.00 pm to 8.00 pm
When you cannot confirm the direction of the approach of an emergency vehicle, you should
Maintain your speed and position.
Increase the speed of your vehicle.
Slow down your speed and move to the left lane.
While driving and you hear the siren of an ambulance behind you, you should
Stop immediately to let the ambulance overtake or pass
Keep left, slow down and stop if necessary
Speed up in order not to obstruct the ambulance
You are not allowed to drive into a bus lane on Monday to Friday from
You can drive on the bus lane
when all other lanes are occupied.
outside the restricted hours.
when passing another vehicle on the left.
When can you use the right lane of a two-lane carriageway?
When your path of travel is obstructed by road works or parked vehicles.
When your speed is higher that the speed limit for the road.
When the right lane is free of traffic.
You may drive along the right-most lane when
You are travelling at the speed limits.
The traffic is not heavy.
You are overtaking another vehicle.
Road hogging
Ensures a smoother flow of traffic
Causes other vehicles to overtake dangerously on the left
Causes other vehicles to overtake on the right
When should you use the right outer most lane of a carriageway?
When driving at the maximum speed
When overtaking
When all other lanes are occupied
You are permitted to use the outer most right lane on a three-lane dual carriageway when
you are travelling at the maximum legal speed limit of the road
you intend to turn right ahead
emergency vehicles are not using it
When you see green traffic light signal from a distance, you should
Speed up.
Slow down.
Carry on at the same speed.
When approaching a traffic light junction with the amber light flashing, you should
Slow down and proceed across the junction only when it is safe to do so.
Speed up in order to pass the junction before the light changes.
Stop at the stop-line and wait for the light to change.
When the traffic light turns green at a junction, you should
depress the accelerator hard and move off quickly.
check traffic from right and left before moving off.
only move off when other vehicles move.
A flashing amber traffic light signal means
signal is about to be cancelled
stop unless you are so close to the stop-line that you cannot stop safety
traffic lights signals are out of order
The light turns red as you approach a traffic junction, when stopping you should
Depress the brake and the clutch pedals simultaneously
Shift to neutral and step on the brakes
Brake firmly and depress the clutch pedal as the car comes to a stop
The 'two-second rule' is used in normal driving situation at
Certain speed only
All speed
Fixed speed only
When approaching a junction and the traffic lights signal change from green to amber, you should
stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
speed up to clear the intersection.
stop only if a red light camera is in use.
When approaching a traffic light signal that has turned to amber, you should
Speed up.
Maintain your speed.
Slow down and stop.
When the amber traffic light is flashing continuously, you should
Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop and wait for it to change to green
Drive through it quickly
When the 'amber' traffic light signal is flashing, you should
Carry on driving
Slow down and look out for other vehicles before proceeding
Call the police
When the traffic light signal turns 'green', you should check
For oncoming traffic before moving off
For oncoming traffic and traffic from the right and left before moving off
The rear view mirror before moving off
When the traffic lights signal turns amber and you have already passed the stop line you should,
stop and reverse back to the stop line
continue to drive through the junction
stop immediately
When the traffic lights signal turns amber, you should
accelerate and cross the junction
slow down and be ready to stop
proceed with caution as the traffic light signals are out of order
When you approach a 'green' traffic light signal at a junction, you should
Accelerate hard
Slow down and be ready to stop
Maintain your speed
Before reaching a junction, you should;
Form up into the correct lane which you intend to travel.
Sound your horn to caution other road users.
Speed up so as not to cause a traffic jam.
On a two-way street with two lanes in each direction, you should keep to;
the left lane.
the outer lane.
either answers.
On a two-lane carriageway, you should
keep to the left lane
keep to the outer lane
not overtake another vehicle
Switching lanes suddenly or abruptly will
improve the flow of traffic on the road.
cause inconvenience and danger to other motorists.
cause wear and tear to the vehicle.
To maintain good lane discipline, you should
form up correctly into the intended lane before reaching the junction
drive between lanes so that you can switch lane easily
follow closely to the vehicle in front
Under what circumstances you may not follow the 'keep left rule' ?
When travelling at the maximum speed limit of the road.
When traffic is light.
When your path is obstructed.
When driving along a two-way street, you should
always keep near the centre line of the road
not cross the centre line at bends
not overtake at all times
When turning right at a one-way street, you should position your vehicle
In the right hand lane.
Just left of the centre of the road.
In any lane depending on the traffic conditions.
You are driving on a three-lane carriageway at 80 km/h .There is no traffic ahead. Which lane should you use ?
Any lane.
Middle lane.
Left lane.
You may overtake another vehicle on the left
If it is a heavy vehicle.
If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.
If you are certain that the vehicle would not change direction.
When should you start to keep left after overtaking?
As soon as you are ahead of the overtaken vehicle.
When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your left wing mirror.
When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.
Before overtaking another vehicle, you should signal for at least
Three seconds
Five seconds
Seven seconds
If a motorcyclist is trying to overtake you, you should
Drive faster to prevent the rider from overtaking you
Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely
Signal the driver to overtake on the left
If the car you are overtaking is drifting in its lane, you should
Use your horn to warn him
Signal him with your hand
Overtake it quickly
To drive in a way where other drivers will not find it necessary to overtake you, you should
Drive on the extreme right lane all the time
Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow
Drive at the maximun speed limit of the road all the time
When a motorcyclist tries to overtake you on the left, you should
Increase your speed to race the rider.
Reduce your speed and assist the rider to overtake safely.
Ignore the rider and continue driving at your normal speed.
When another vehicle is overtaking you, you should
not speed up but assist him to overtake
change lane and keep to the right
increase your speed gradually
When being overtaken, you should
speed up
maintain your speed
slow down
When the motorcycle you are overtaking suddenly increases speed, you should
accelerate more to overtake it quickly
slow down and abort overtaking it
sound your horn to warn the driver
When you have moved to the right hand side of the road to overtake another vehicle, you should
Maintain your normal speed and overtake as usual
Accelerate and overtake as quickly as possible
Decelerate and change to a higher gear
While overtaking another vehicle, the vehicle suddenly goes faster, you should
accelerate hard to overtake quickly
slow down and move safely back to your lane
sound the horn continuously to warn the other driver
Driving with a 'bald' tyre is dangerous because
it skids more easily.
there is greater probability of punctures.
both answers (A) and (B).
When you are driving along, you must check your rear view mirror once every
1 to 2 seconds.
5 to 10 seconds.
20 to 30 seconds.
Reversing from a side road into a main road is
Allowed if there is no vehicle around.
Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.
Allowed during the daytime only.
Crossing the double continuous white lines along the centre of the road
Is an offence because it is unsafe to do so.
Is not an offence if you are overtaking another vehicle.
Is not an offence if you do not cause inconvenience to others.
No parking is allowed within ___ metres of a junction
12 metres of a junction.
6 metres of a junction.
9 metres of a junction.
Parking of vehicle is prohibited within __ metres of a bus stop.
15 metres of a bus stop.
12 metres of a bus stop.
9 metres of a bus stop.
When approaching a sharp bend or a steep hill, you
Should not overtake other vehicles.
May overtake other vehicles.
Should stay close behind the front vehicle.
When the vehicle you are overtaking suddenly increases its speed, you should
Increase your speed further.
Sound the horn and signal the driver to slow down.
Reduce your speed and return to your original lane.
In traffic hold-ups, you should
try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the right.
try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the left.
stay in queue and follow the traffic flow.
When you see a vehicle slowing down before a Zebra Crossing, you should
slow down and be prepared to stop.
sound the horn and signal the driver to slow down.
maintain your speed.
Road hogging
allows others to overtake safely.
holds up the flow of traffic.
reduces road accident.
You want to reverse into a side road. You are not sure that the area behind your vehicle is clear. What should you do?
carry on, assuming it is clear.
look through the rear window only.
get out and check.
Before entering a round about, you should
Give way to traffic on your right.
Stop first before entering.
Accelerate to merge smoothly with traffic already in the roundabout.
A tyre needs to be changed when
It is two years old.
The depth of its tread is less than 1.6 mm.
It is completely bald.
The minimum age requirement for applying for a Basic Theory Test is
16 years.
17 years.
18 years.
Unless otherwise stated, the maximum speed limit of all roads in Singapore is
50km/h.
60km/h.
80km/h.
When driving in the rain, you should
Drive faster to get home.
Reduce your speed.
Drive at normal speed.
When driving pass pedestrians or cyclists, you should
Drive at normal speed, close to them.
Slow down and always give ample side clearance.
Drive quickly past them.
When following a bus that pulls up at a bus stop, you should
accelerate past the bus quickly.
slow down and watch carefully for pedestrians.
sound the horn and overtake the bus.
When the 'Red man' signal is on and pedestrians are crossing, you should
horn the pedestrians to demand the right of way.
stop and allow pedestrians to cross.
proceed behind the pedestrians.
When you see children standing by the side of the road, you should
maintain your normal speed.
slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
speed pass them.
You are driving pass a line of parked cars. You notice a ball bouncing out into the road ahead, you should
Continue driving at the same speed and sound your horn.
Slow down and be prepared to stop for children.
Continue driving at the same speed and try to avoid the ball.
You are turning left into a side road. Pedestrians are crossing the road near the junction. You should
Wave them on.
Wait for them to cross.
Sound your horn.
You need a longer distance to stop your vehicle when driving
On a dry road.
On a wet road.
On a hard and dry ground.
You see two elderly pedestrians about to cross the road ahead, you should
Expect them to wait for you to pass.
Speed up to pass them quickly.
Be careful, they may misjudge your speed.
How does alcohol affect you?
It reduces your concentration.
It increases your awareness.
It improves your co-ordination.
Drink driving
will not affect your reaction time.
may affect your reaction time.
may cause you to react faster.
Which of the following statements on alcohol and driving is true?
It is safe to drive as long as you think you are not drunk.
It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.
It is safe to drive one hour after having the last drink.
A person will be disqualified from driving if he is caught
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of blood.
Failing to obey a 'Stop' traffic sign.
Failing to give way to an ambulance with its siren on.
A driver caught with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood will
have to pay a fine.
be charged in court.
be jailed.
After consuming alcohol, you should
not drive.
drive slowly.
drive at normal speed.
Any person caught driving with blood alcohol content which exceeds the prescribed limit will
have to pay a fine.
be charged in court.
be given a warning.
Drink driving may cause
Reduce the co-ordination of the control of vehicle.
Faster reaction.
Increase alertness.
Drinking and driving may cause
Increase confidence.
Loss of proper control of the vehicle.
Greater awareness of danger.
Generally, a small amount of alcohol can make you less safe on the road.
True.
False.
Not true, if you were an experience driver.
How does the consumption of alcohol affect a person's driving?
It enables the driver to make better judgements.
It enables the driver to have better vision of the road.
It reduces the driver's reaction.
If you failed to have a proper control of your vehicle, you could be charged for _______________ even though your blood alcohol content is below the legal limit.
Careless driving.
Drink driving.
Reckless driving.
If you consume alcohol, you should
Have a coffee then drive home.
Go home by public transport.
Drive home carefully.
If you had too much alcohol,
your ability to drive is impaired.
Your reactions are better.
Your vision is improved.
If you intend to drive after attending a function, you should
Avoid mixing your alcoholic drinks .
Avoid drinking alcohol.
Drink coffee before drinking alcohol.
The penalty for a repeat drink driving offender is
Fine, disqualification and a mandatory jail sentence.
Disqualification only.
Fine and disqualification only.
Drink driving can contribute to accidents because
Driver's judgement is impaired.
Drivers take shorter time to react.
Driver's vision is improved.
What advice should you give to a driver who has a few alcoholic drinks at a party?
Drive home carefully and slowly.
Go home by public transport.
Wait a short while and then drive home.
Which of the following sentences is TRUE?
Alcohol makes you a better driver.
Alcohol has no effect on the way you drive.
Alcohol slows down your reactions when driving.
Which of the following statement on alcohol is true?
You may decline a breath or blood test
Alcohol will not be detected by the breath test after peppermints have been eaten.
Even a small amount of alcohol tends to increase the chance of an accident.
Which of these can affect your reaction time?
Drugs
Contact lenses.
Tinted windows.
A passenger is exempted from wearing a seat belt if he is below
1.7 metres in height.
1.6 metres in height.
1.5 metres in height.
Children passenger below _____ of age are required to use a child restraint.
10 years.
9 years.
8 years.
Fastening a seat belt can
Reduce the chances of a collision.
Reduce the chances of being seriously injured or killed.
Control your body movement when you negotiate a sharp bend.
Seat belt must be worn at all times by
the driver only.
the passengers only.
the driver as well as the passengers.
A child is required to use a child restraint if the child is
7 years old.
9 years old.
11 years old.
The 'Two-second Rule' is a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the car in front when road condition is
Wet.
Good.
Hazy.
You are on a clear and open road in good weather condition, the distance between you and the vehicle in front should be
one car's length.
two car's length.
a two second time gap.
The Two-second Rule is a simple check to ensure
A safe distance for you to move off from a junction.
A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.
A safe length of time to signal before your manoeuvre.
When you are following another vehicle on a wet road, you should keep
2 seconds behind.
More than 2 seconds behind.
Less than 2 seconds behind.
The 'Two-Second Rule' of safe following distance applies to all vehicles travelling at
slow speed only.
fast speed only.
any speed.
In order to avoid an accident with the vehicle in front while driving under normal conditions you should use the
Two-second rule
Four-second rule
Two metre rule
After driving through flood the brakes may malfunction. In order to correct this, you must
Stop the vehicle on a slope to allow water to flow out from the brakes.
Pump the brake pedal repeatedly to dry the brakes.
Drive at normal speed to spin-dry the brakes.
After your vehicle passed through a flood, you should
stop on a slope to drain water out of the brakes.
drive faster to allow the brakes to dry quickly.
apply intermittent braking to dry the brake drums at low speed.
How should you deal with floods?
Drive through as fast as possible to avoid stopping.
Drive through slowly in 1st gear.
Drive through in the highest gear.
If you are in doubt of the depth of flood water (whether passable to vehicles), you should
Drive through slowly.
Drive through as quickly as possible.
Take an alternative route.
To drive through a flood, you should increase acceleration and
Change to a lower gear.
Change to a higher gear.
Apply half clutch.
When approaching a road that is flooded but passable to vehicles, you should
Engage a higher gear to go through the flood.
Engage a lower gear to go through the flood.
Drive through as fast as possible.
When driving in heavy rain and passing through water, you should gently test your
horn.
brakes from time to time.
signals.
All drivers are required by law to switch on the vehicle's headlights whilst driving between
7.00 pm and 7.00 am.
7.15 pm and 7.15 am.
7.30 pm and 7.30 am.
Switching on the headlights whilst driving in heavy rain during the daytime
Is advisable because you can be readily seen by others.
Is not advisable because it will shorten the battery life.
Is not advisable because the rain water will reflect the light.
At night, when approaching a sharp left bend you should
Flash your headlights to attract the attention of other road user.
Speed up so as to pass the danger as quickly as possible.
Keep more to the right to have a better view.
If the headlight of an oncoming vehicle is blinding you, you should
turn on the high beam.
look to the right kerb.
look to the left kerb.
At night you should switch on your headlights from
6 pm to 7 am
7 pm to 6 am
7 pm to 7 am
In which situation should you switch on the high beam?
When driving on a bumpy road
When there are oncoming vehicles
When the road is poorly lighted and there is no traffic ahead
On a sharp bend at night, to avoid dazzling oncoming traffic, you should
Switch off your lights.
Dip your headlights.
Switch on high beam.
The purpose of using dipped headlights whilst driving is to
to save the battery's electrical energy.
to light up the road immediately in front of you.
to avoid dazzling drivers of oncoming vehicles.
When blinded by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle at night, you should
Close your eyes.
Slow down or stop.
Pull down the sun visor.
When driving at night, dip your headlights-
To light up the road immediately in front you.
So as not to dazzle drivers of oncoming vehicles.
To prolong the life of the car battery.
When driving at night, you should use
Dipped headlights.
High beam.
Side lights only.
When facing oncoming traffic at night, which lights should you use?
Dipped headlights.
High beam headlights.
Spot lights.
When the oncoming car refuses to dim its headlights, you should
Slow down and look at the left side of the kerb
Retaliate by turning on your high beam.
Maintain your speed and the headlight status.
You should dip your headlights when
Driving in a dark area.
Facing oncoming traffic.
Approaching a blind corner.
